subject: Commercial pricing clarification: slab + hot-reserve SKU model

Subject: Commercial pricing clarification: slab + hot-reserve SKU model

Hiro / Marissa / Rishi,

Thanks for the initial RFP response — we've reviewed the commercial section and have a few clarifying questions before we include your pricing in the shortlist. Key items where we need concrete language and an example calculation: 

1) Slab pricing bands: you list bands (0-50M, 50-200M tokens, etc.) but the RFP needs per-1k-token effective unit prices and clear cutoff rules (are bands applied pro-rata or bucketed?). Please confirm.

2) Hot-reserve (burst) SKU: we like the idea of a separate hot-reserve pool for peak traffic. How do you price this? Hourly seat vs. reserved token buffer vs. per-token overage — need a preferred commercial construct and whether unused reserved hot capacity can be credited/rolled over.

3) True-up and billing cadence: monthly true-up or quarterly? How are refunds/credits handled if committed capacity is underutilized? Any minimum monthly invoice?

4) Model tiers: does per-token pricing vary by model class (base vs. instruction-tuned vs. embedding)? Provide a short matrix.

5) SLA credits & canary clause: for enterprise procurement we need an example clause and impact on pricing if SLA misses occur.

Attached: RFP_Commercial_Section_v3.pdf — contains the RFP form where answers should be placed.

Can we get a written clarification and a short worked example (3-month usage with peaks) by end of Tuesday? If it's easier we can do a 30m sync.

Thanks,
Samantha

Samantha — following up with the commercial responses in-line below. Putting the short version here; Rishi will attach a worked 3-month scenario with exact math in his next note.

Summary (short answers)
- Slab bands: we price on a pro-rata basis across bands (not bucketed). Effective per-1k-token price is calculated by summing charges per band. See table below.
- Hot-reserve SKU: recommended construct is a hybrid — a small hourly "hot seat" reservation (for guaranteed concurrency) priced hourly + a per-token burst allowance for the pooled bursts. Unused burst allowances convert to credits at 25% of list value and can be rolled forward for up to 2 billing cycles.
- True-up cadence: monthly true-up with quarterly invoicing available upon request for enterprise contracts. Underutilization credits applied monthly; minimum invoice = $5,000/month for committed plans.
- Model tiers: generation models and embeddings are priced differently; embeddings billed per-1k vectors (or per-1k tokens if using tokenized embedding pipelines).
- SLA & canary: SLA credits capped at 20% of monthly invoice; canary clause (30-day trial of production traffic on a reduced commit) available for new deployments.

Representative pricing table (text):
- Band A: 0 - 50M tokens -> $0.009 per 1k tokens
- Band B: 50M - 250M tokens -> $0.0065 per 1k tokens
- Band C: 250M - 1B tokens -> $0.0042 per 1k tokens
- Band D: 1B+ tokens -> $0.0033 per 1k tokens (reserved commit pricing)

Hot-reserve SKU (recommended)
- Hot seat reservation: $1.25 per reserved hot seat per hour (billed monthly). Each reserved hot seat includes 200k burst tokens per month.
- Per-token overage from hot pool: $0.007 per 1k tokens for generation models; $0.012 per 1k tokens for embeddings.
- Unused hot allowance credit: converted at 25% value, rollover up to 2 cycles.

True-up example notes (short)
- Monthly usage is measured at invoice close. If usage < committed tokens, customer gets credit at the committed effective rate pro-rated. If usage > committed tokens, overage priced at blended banded rates plus hot-reserve overage where applicable.

Contractual nuances
- Minimum commitment: 6 months for hot-reserve SKU; 12 months for large reserved commit discounts.
- Early termination: remaining committed credit converts to a 60% early termination charge unless replaced by equivalent commit.

Attachment: commercial-terms-summary.docx (this file contains the same table plus legal-friendly wording for the RFP).

If that matches what you need, we'll send the 3-month worked example and a redlined suggested RFP response.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial GTM
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — that's helpful. A couple of clarifying questions before we finalize the RFP section: 

1) The unused hot allowance credit at 25% looks low for us — can you explain why not 50% or full rollover? Is there a commercial option to increase the credit in exchange for a longer commitment?

2) For the hourly hot seat: if we reserve 10 seats but only use spikes for one hour a day, is the monthly economics better than just buying burst per-token credits? We need a 3-month example comparing: (A) no hot-seat, per-token overage only; (B) 10 hot seats reserved; (C) short-term on-demand burst units. Please include model mix (60% gen-large, 40% embeddings) and regional pricing in US.

3) Canary: can the 30-day canary live inside the committed window (i.e., count toward the first month of commit) or is it separate?

We can do the 30m call Wed 6/24 10:00 PT if that helps.

Best,
Samantha
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Commercial pricing clarification: slab + hot-reserve SKU model

Samantha — attaching the 3-month worked scenario as requested; summary below. Attachment: 3month-scenario-calculation.csv

Worked example (summary, 3 months): assumptions -> month1 baseline 180M tokens, month2 baseline 210M tokens (mid-month peak +50M tokens), month3 baseline 130M tokens with 2 short spikes (combined +80M tokens). Model mix: 60% generation-large, 40% embeddings.

Option A: No hot-seat (overage only) - Banded charges (pro-rata across bands) result in an average blended per-1k price ~ $0.0058 after band progression; overage tokens priced at $0.007 (gen) / $0.012 (embeds) when above reserved commit.

Option B: 10 hot seats reserved (hourly price) - Cost: 10 seats * $1.25/hr * 24 * 30 = $9,000/month (approx). Each seat includes 200k burst tokens/month -> 10 seats = 2M burst tokens (useful for small sustained peaks). In months with large spikes the blended cost (seat + overage) results in 12-18% lower spend vs. Option A in our scenario.

Option C: On-demand bursts (no seats) - All burst handled as per-token overage. For the 3-month pattern Option C is 6–10% more expensive than Option B and roughly 4% cheaper than Option A in month3 only; variability depends on spike shape.

Unused hot allowances: we set 25% credit as a conservative commercial amortization (helps us balance reserved empty capacity). We can increase credit to 40% with a 24-month commit or to 60% with a 36-month commit — happy to include a tiered rollover credit option in the contract.

Canary clause: canary can be inside the committed window and count toward month-1 usage provided volume thresholds are met and traffic is gated to a single region. We'll formalize the clause in RFP language.

HubSpot reference: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/8764 (DEAL-8764)

If this summary looks right we'll send the CSV with line-by-line math and a redlined commercial paragraph for insertion into the RFP.

Regards,
